acceptanceCriteria: Repositories using the tri-language reference-parity convention reject a new active Work Item with a missing, symlinked, or malformed own projection before expensive verification can start.
The rejection identifies the exact page or parity file and reason, remains fail-closed, and does not write terminal lifecycle state.
Repositories without the declared parity convention retain existing generic lifecycle behavior.
Regression coverage proves missing projection is rejected early, valid prearchive projection passes, and post-close promotion remains current.
No existing historical evidence or release artifact is rewritten.
The first-start and workflow projections explicitly distinguish same-root amend/revalidate/retry from an explicitly bound successor, and regression coverage preserves that rule.
goal: Add a Runtime-enforced, repository-aware prearchive documentation projection precondition for repositories that declare the tri-language parity convention; reject missing or malformed own pages before checkpoint/verification and before close, emit concrete paths and reasons, and add regression coverage and operator documentation.
intent: Prevent the recurring post-close documentation projection failure at the earliest lifecycle boundary while preserving generic object-project behavior.
